title: Parse a number from text
description:
Turn the characters of a line into a number yourself.

```
Text: -1234
parsed: -1234, doubled: -2468
Text: 12ab
not a number at position 3
```

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
ask:    db      "Text: ", 0

        section .bss
line:   resb    64

        section .text
_start:
        lea     rdi, [rel ask]
        call    print_str
        lea     rdi, [rel line]
        mov     esi, 64
        call    read_line
        ; TODO

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: `imul rbx, rbx, 10` / `movzx eax, byte [r12 + rcx]` / `sub eax, '0'` / `add rbx, rax` (lesson 6.02).
`cmp al, 9` / `ja .bad` after subtracting `'0'` catches every non-digit with one unsigned comparison.
requirements: Read the line with `read_line`, then parse it without `read_int`: an optional `-`, then digits.
Multiply the total by 10 and add each digit (`sub al, '0'`).
A character that is not a digit prints its position (1-based).
stretch: Detect overflow with `jo` after the multiply and the add.
